forces: A duplicate installed copy is a packaging fault and must be reported as such, but only in wording: the rejection itself never changes and no authority is ever granted either way.
The frozen contract already reserves DUPLICATE_AUTHORITY in validation_error_codes; no contract amendment and no regeneration may be proposed.
No public API change and no new SDK error code: the diagnostic reuses the reserved code with the bounded code/category/path shape.
The cross-copy channel must stay diagnostic-only: boolean predicates, never registry membership, brands, values, or foreign-authority acceptance.
The probe must not create a new crash surface: foreign predicates are try/catch-wrapped and coerced to boolean, and a hostile sibling can at most soften wording.
The scope gate must admit globalThis for exactly the probe module without weakening the globalThis ban anywhere else.
The message must name the single-copy invariant verbatim (#86 wording) and name deduplication as the remediation, as one coordinated wording reused by #86's fixture.
Forged, cast, and cloned values keep AUTHORITY_ESCALATION; the escalation/duplicate contrast is the point of issue #79's acceptance criteria 1 and 2.
Sibling and nested duplication share one code because nothing observable distinguishes npm-installed duplication from an attacker's second copy; the security decision never changes.
#79's classification must land as its own compatibility.json patch[] entry without touching #78's historical entry, and ADR-SDK-004 gains a dated amendment without changing the decision.

forces: The cross-copy channel must stay diagnostic-only: boolean predicates, never registry membership, brands, values, or foreign-authority acceptance.
approach-global-registry-singleton.reason: A globalThis-anchored shared registry is reachable and mutable by any code in the process, would make copy B accept copy A's brands, and violates the issue's own constraint that detection cannot accept foreign authority. It was explicitly rejected by the #78 assessment and ADR-SDK-004 invariant 7, and it is not re-proposed in probe clothing: the diagnostic-only probe shares booleans, never membership, and the value is rejected either way.

forces: The frozen contract already reserves DUPLICATE_AUTHORITY in validation_error_codes; no contract amendment and no regeneration may be proposed.
approach-contract-amendment-new-code.reason: DUPLICATE_AUTHORITY is already a reserved member of the frozen contract's validation_error_codes and is referenced nowhere in src/ outside the generated list, so the dedicated diagnostic is already provisioned. A contract amendment would trip changed-path verification and make contract/sdk mutually unsatisfiable (the exact trap PR #259 resolved), and a new SDK error code would be a public API change this issue neither needs nor asks for.

security_justification.audit_integrity: Rejection behavior is unchanged; only the operator-facing code and message of an already-rejecting path change, so no event can reach the sink through this diagnostic.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: No authority grant changes: the value is rejected either way, and the probe's answer never turns a rejection into acceptance.
security_justification.authority_provenance: Registry membership stays module-private and insertion stays constructor-only; the probe reports a sibling's membership as a boolean only, and never transmits brands, values, or membership itself.
security_justification.concurrency: The probe adds one append-only registration array per resolved module copy; registration is idempotent per copy and introduces no mutable shared state beyond the boolean channel.
security_justification.confidentiality: No caller data, event payload, secret, or raw error crosses copies; the DUPLICATE_AUTHORITY rejection carries code, category, and bounded path only, serialized under 512 bytes.
security_justification.cryptography: No cryptographic primitive, key material, hash, signature, or cryptographic trust assumption changes.
security_justification.error_disclosure: The bounded shape is preserved and the message names the invariant and the remediation without adding payload, stack, or secret content; toJSON() stays {code, category, path}.
security_justification.external_security_integration: No exporter, collector, SIEM, transport, browser telemetry, analytics, detection, or external security service is introduced or authorized.
security_justification.fail_posture: Forged, cast, cloned, sibling-duplicate, and nested-duplicate values all fail closed before the sink; the wording differs, the rejection does not.
security_justification.lifecycle: No initialization, shutdown, delivery, queue, retry, or persistence behavior changes.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: This change owns the diagnostic wording, the probe channel, the fixture tightening, and the compatibility/ADR records; #86 owns the single-copy Core proof and dependency-gate rescoping.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: No personal, browser, client, event, or derived data is collected, transformed, retained, or exposed.
security_justification.resource_retention: The module-private WeakMap ownership model is unchanged; the probe's append-only array grows by one entry per resolved module copy, which is bounded by the number of copies and carries no values.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: The change adds no delivery, retry, redelivery, queue, buffering, or durability behavior.
security_justification.trust_boundary: The probe is diagnostic-only and never accepts foreign authority; a hostile in-process sibling can at most soften the operator-facing wording, and that bounded limitation is recorded rather than compensated by weakening the rejection.
